critique.feedback: Labels, relationship name/direction (AccountHolder-[:HAS_CREDITCARD]->CreditCard) and property owner (c.balance on CreditCard) are all correct, and no filter is needed. The mismatch is grain inconsistency between the two aggregates: MATCH ... RETURN produces one row per (AccountHolder, CreditCard) pair, so avg(c.balance) averages over holder-card holdings and weights each card by how many holders link to it, while count(DISTINCT c) collapses to distinct CreditCard identities. Since the schema allows a CreditCard to be the end of multiple HAS_CREDITCARD relationships, a card shared by two holders would contribute its balance twice to the average yet be counted once in the total. Both requested figures are stated at the CreditCard grain ('average balance of CreditCards', 'total number of CreditCards'), so deduplicate card identity before aggregating in both measures — e.g. MATCH (a:AccountHolder)-[:HAS_CREDITCARD]->(c:CreditCard) WITH DISTINCT c RETURN avg(c.balance) AS averageBalance, count(c) AS totalCreditCards. If instead the intent were an average over holdings, drop the DISTINCT from the count so both aggregates share the same grain.
